question.problem: Suppose that $|\,c\,|=\sqrt{2}$, $|\,d\,|=6$ and that the angle between the vectors is $\theta ={45}^{∘}.$ Find the vector projection of $d$ onto $c$ in terms of the vector $c.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the scalar projection as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{comp}}_{c}\,d & =|\,d\,|\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =6\operatorname{cos}⁡({45}^{∘}) \\  & =6\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\  & =3\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the unit vector that is parallel to $c:$

$$
u=\frac{c}{|\,c\,|}=\frac{c}{\sqrt{2}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}c
$$

Finally, we compute the vector projection as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{c}\,d & ={\text{comp}}_{c}\,d\cdot u \\  & =3\sqrt{2}\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}c \\  & =3c\end{aligned}
$$
